children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning an eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I've started the assessment. To begin, I need to know about your child or children.

**How old is the child you're claiming for?**

Please let me know:
- The age(s) of your child or children
- The name(s) of the child or children

This will help me guide you through the right eligibility checks. 

For context:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualifies automatically
- **16-19**: May qualify if they're in approved education or training
- **20 or older**: Generally doesn't qualify

Who am I assessing for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex - he's 17 years old and lives at home with me. I want to make sure I can still claim for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thanks for that information! It's great that you're checking your eligibility. Let me work through this with you.

So you're looking to claim for **Alex, who is 17 years old**. Since Alex is in the 16-19 age range, I need to check whether he qualifies based on his education or training status.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

For example:
- Full-time school, college, or university
- Full-time apprenticeship
- Full-time vocational training
- Other approved training schemes

Please let me know what Alex is doing at the moment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually left school recently, but he's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next. He's still working out his options at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thanks for that clarification! So Alex has recently left school and is currently registered with the local careers service while working out his next steps.

This is important because there's a potential extension period for young people who've just left education. Let me check if Alex qualifies under that extension eligibility.

**A couple of quick questions to clarify his situation:**

1. **When did Alex leave school?** (Roughly how many weeks ago - was it within the last 20 weeks?)

2. **Is he registered with a careers service, Jobcentre Plus, or a similar approved service** while looking for work or training?

3. **Is he actively seeking education, training, or employment?**

These details will help me determine if he falls within the extension period that allows Child Benefit to continue after leaving full-time education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I can see that there's a **20-week extension available** for young people like Alex who've recently left education and registered with a qualifying service.

To determine if Alex qualifies for this extension, I need you to confirm:

1. **Did Alex leave school within the last 20 weeks?** (Roughly, is it recent - say within the last 5 months?)

2. **Is he registered with one of these qualifying services:**
   - Government Careers Service
   - Connexions
   - Armed Services

Once you confirm these details, I can work through the rest of the eligibility checks with you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he left school within the last 20 weeks - it's been fairly recent. And yes, he's registered with the careers service like I mentioned. He's just in that period where he's trying to work out what to do next, you know?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So Alex meets the extension criteria - he's left school within the last 20 weeks and is registered with the careers service. That means he can continue to qualify for Child Benefit during this 20-week period while he's figuring out his next steps.

Now let me move to the next check. Since Alex is in this extension period, I need to verify that **he's not working full-time**.

**Is Alex working full-time (or do you anticipate he will be)?**

For context, "full-time work" typically means 24 hours or more per week on a regular basis. Part-time work or occasional work wouldn't disqualify him during this extension period.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all at the moment. He's just focused on working out what he wants to do - whether that's college, an apprenticeship, or something else. No job right now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex isn't working full-time (or at all), so he passes this check. Let me continue with the next eligibility requirement.

**Is Alex currently receiving any benefits in his own right?**

For example:
- Income Support
- Jobseeker's Allowance (JSA)
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (as a claimant in his own right, not as a dependent)

This is just to confirm he's not already receiving certain state benefits that would affect Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name. He's still living at home with me and isn't claiming anything himself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own right, so he passes that check too.

Now, let me ask one more question about Alex's specific situation:

**Is Alex an apprentice (i.e., enrolled in an apprenticeship programme)?**

This is just to clarify his status, as apprenticeships are treated slightly differently in the eligibility rules.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not doing an apprenticeship. Like I said, he's just registered with the careers service working out what he wants to do next - whether that might be college, an apprenticeship in the future, or getting a job. But right now he's not in anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex is not currently in an apprenticeship, so he passes that check as well.

Now let me move to the next important eligibility requirement. I need to check some details about **you** as the claimant:

**What is your residency status?** Specifically:

1. **Where do you live?** (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland?)

2. **What is your immigration or residency status?** For example:
   - British citizen
   - EU citizen (and if so, do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?)
   - Other visa holder
   - Asylum seeker

This information is important because Child Benefit has specific residency and immigration requirements for the person claiming.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see there are several possible residency paths. Let me simplify this for you:

**To help me check your residency eligibility, could you tell me:**

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)

2. **Are you a British citizen, or do you have another residency status?** (For example, EU citizen with settled/pre-settled status, or other visa status)

This will help me determine which residency requirement applies to you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. And I'm a British citizen, so there shouldn't be any issues with residency or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! You're a British citizen living in the UK (Manchester), so you definitely meet the residency requirements. That's straightforward.

Now let me move to the next important check:

**Are you responsible for Alex?** 

In other words:
- Do you have day-to-day responsibility for caring for Alex?
- Does he live with you?
- Are you his parent or legal guardian?

I'm asking because Child Benefit is only payable to the person who has main responsibility for the child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely - I'm his mum and he lives at home with me. I look after him day-to-day, so yes, I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! You're Alex's mum, he lives at home with you, and you have day-to-day responsibility for him. That clearly meets the responsibility requirement.

Now, let me check one more important thing:

**Is there anyone else who might also be claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there any dispute about who should be claiming for him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's father also potentially claiming for him?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent or other relative) claiming for him?
- Has there been any change in circumstances that might affect this?

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, and if there's more than one potential claimant, HMRC may need to make a decision about who is entitled.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's nobody else claiming for him. It's just me - I'm the only one looking after him and I'd be the only one claiming.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! So there's no other claimant for Alex - just you. That's clear.

Now, let me check the final important details about Alex's location:

**Where does Alex normally live?**

Specifically:
- Does he live with you in the UK most of the time?
- Is he temporarily abroad, or does he spend time in other countries?
- Has he moved away from the UK permanently or for an extended period?

Child Benefit eligibility depends on where the child is normally residing.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me here in Manchester. He's not abroad or anything - he's just at home with me full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex lives with you at home in Manchester full-time. That's the normal living arrangement.

Just to complete the eligibility check, I need to confirm a couple of final details:

**1. Is Alex currently in hospital?**

**2. Is Alex in local authority care or a care home?**

**3. Is Alex fostered?**

These are just to check if any special circumstances apply. Since you've said he's living at home with you, I expect the answer to all of these would be "no", but I want to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No to all of those - he's not in hospital, not in care, and not fostered. He's just living at home with me like a normal 17-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's clear - Alex is living at home with you in a normal living arrangement, not in any special circumstances.

Now, just one final check before I can give you my assessment:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's upkeep or maintenance?**

For example, is the council contributing financially to his care or living costs?

(In most cases, this would be "no", but I need to confirm this last detail to complete the eligibility assessment.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards him. I'm covering all his costs myself - it's just a normal family situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final piece of information I need. Let me now provide you with my eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! 🎉

## **You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

Based on everything you've told me, you meet all the eligibility requirements. Here's why:

**For Alex (age 17):**
- ✅ He's in the 16-19 age range and has left school within the last 20 weeks
- ✅ He's registered with the careers service (a qualifying service) during this transition period
- ✅ He's not working full-time (24+ hours per week)
- ✅ He's not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✅ He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ He lives at home with you full-time

**For you (the claimant):**
- ✅ You're a British citizen living in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You have day-to-day responsibility for Alex and live with him
- ✅ You're the only person claiming for him
- ✅ The local council is not paying towards his upkeep

---

## **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. You'll need to provide:
   - Proof of your identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Details about your family situation

3. **Important note about High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you (or a partner, if you have one) earns over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge, which can reduce or eliminate the benefit
   - Child Benefit is currently **£25.60 per week** (or £111.40 per week for the eldest/only child)

4. **Payment frequency:**
   - Payments are usually made every 4 weeks
   - If you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits, payments may be weekly

---

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?
